title: The Image of God
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The image of God means that human beings are created by God with unique dignity, worth, responsibility, and purpose before Him. Every person bears God-given value, even though sin has damaged humanity and Christ alone restores people to God’s intended purpose.
summary: The image of God means that human beings are created by God with unique dignity, worth, responsibility, and purpose before Him. Every person bears God-given value, even though sin has damaged humanity and Christ alone restores people to God’s intended purpose.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the perfect image of God and the true man who restores fallen people. Through Him, believers are renewed in knowledge, righteousness, and holiness, being conformed to the image of the Son.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Human dignity begins with God. People are not valuable because of strength, intelligence, health, productivity, status, usefulness, appearance, approval, or ability. Human beings have worth because God created them in His image.

The image of God sets humanity apart from the rest of creation. People were made to know God, reflect His character, exercise stewardship, live in relationship, and walk under His authority. Human life is therefore sacred and must be treated with reverence.

Sin has damaged the image of God in humanity, but it has not erased human worth. People still bear God’s image, even in weakness, disability, suffering, age, poverty, addiction, failure, or rejection. No person is disposable before God.

Christ restores what sin has broken. He is the perfect image of God, and those who belong to Him are being renewed after His likeness. The Gospel does not merely forgive sinners; it restores people toward the purpose for which they were created.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People who feel unwanted, disabled, rejected, forgotten, or treated as less valuable need to know their worth is not assigned by society, productivity, appearance, health, income, or approval. Human dignity begins with God, not with what a person can perform or prove.

This doctrine also confronts the way people mistreat themselves and others. No person is disposable. No person is beyond concern. Every human life must be approached with reverence because every person bears the mark of the Creator, even though that image needs restoration through Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: See people through the truth of creation and redemption. Refuse to measure yourself or others by usefulness, strength, status, disability, past failure, or social acceptance. Honor God’s image in the overlooked, protect the vulnerable, repent of contempt, and let Christ teach you to treat people with holy dignity and sacrificial love.
